messages.subject: ar1 with panel data
parts:
Does INLA's ar(1) effect work correctly when the data
contains multiple instances of each time variable? There's
a discussion in Blangiardo+Cameletti which suggests that
it should (in the context of the rw(1) model, not ar(1))
but I'm not sure.

Consider the example in the ar1.pdf write-up. Here we
have a sample of 100 observations. Supose now that we
stack copies of the dataset, so that we work with 200 and
then 300 observations.  I'd expect that the resulting
estimates would be similar, but what I get is
(for the means, sd's in parens):

Num. Obs.   Intercept       prec(z)        rho
True                        10.00         0.80
100       .1493 (.11)   6.67 (2.09    0.70 (.11)
200           .1251 (.10)   4.54 (1.03)   0.55 (.11)
300           .1129 (.09)   3.93 (0.79)   0.48 (.11)

To me it looks as if the larger the sample size,
the further away from the true values the estimates
become. Is this what experts would expect? Maybe
my intuitions are just wrong. Or am
I doing something wrong, and there's something else
I need to do in order to correctly implement an ar(1)
random effects structure when I have a panel dataset?

[PS- the writeup for rw(1) says that it has an example
illustrating the use of the values parameter. Best I
can see, it doesn't].


Thanks for any help/advice!

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] ar1 with panel data
parts:
On Tue, 2017-11-07 at 10:05 -0800, vit...@osu.edu wrote:
>
>
> Does INLA's ar(1) effect work correctly when the data
> contains multiple instances of each time variable? There's
> a discussion in Blangiardo+Cameletti which suggests that
> it should (in the context of the rw(1) model, not ar(1))
> but I'm not sure.

it should do, as multiple observation is 'standard'. it might be an issue with
locations, as

f(time, model = "ar1")

is 'not time' in itself, like time = 1, 2, 3, but indexing to and argument 'values'
that defines the locations, and by default it is the values of 'time'. so that


> r = inla(y ~ -1 + f(time, model="ar1"), control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 10, fixed=TRUE))), data = data.frame(y = y, time = 1:10))
> rr = inla(y ~ -1 + f(time, model="ar1"), control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 10, fixed=TRUE))), data = data.frame(y = y, time = (1:10)^2))


is the same. if you want the ar1 from 1, 2, ..., 100, you must add

values = 1:100

in the f(time, ....)


could this be it?

Thanks for your very quick reply! I'm not sure I get it, so maybe I should post my code. (This is for the base and 200 observations cases only).

# set up the problem, per ar1.pdf
library(INLA)
set.seed(1234)

n<-100
rho<-0.8
prec<-10

E<-sample(c(5,4,10,12),size=n,replace=T)
eta<-as.vector(arima.sim(list(order=c(1,0,0),ar=rho),n=n,sd=sqrt(1/prec)))
y<-rpois(n,E*exp(eta))
z<-1:n
data<-data.frame(y=y,z=z,E=E)
# data$z is 1,2,...,100

# now run inla. Note that adding the control.family per HR's reply doesn't change anything in this case.

formula<-y~f(z,model="ar1")
result<-inla(formula,family="poisson",data=data,E=E)
summary(result)
# here intercept =  .1493 (.11)   prec(z)= 6.655 (2.09)   rho = .6969 (.11)

# now the doubling up of the data
data2<-rbind(data,data)
result2<-inla(formula,family="poisson",data=data2,E=E)
summary(result2)
# here intercept = .1251 (.10) prec(z) = 4.54 (1.03)   rho = .5495 (.11)
# data2$z is 1,2,...,100,1,2,...,100

Does this help see what's going on?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] ar1 with panel data
parts:
Two things:
I would use E=data2$E instead of E=E to know that the correct E is used.
You are repeating the same observations instead of adding new ones based on the same latent process. I would expect this to lead to an estimate of the latent process adapted to the specific random y sample you first generated, instead of converging to the true realisation of the latent process (and I’d expect some effect of that on the rho estimate as well).

Finn
